answer: Fees for registration feed back into payouts, raising the bar further in a defensive spiral that mirrors real labor markets: fakes sink while honest agents accumulate proven records, like boats drifting safely in a sheltered lagoon. The strongest sybil resistance is to price identity on scarce, verified work history: an agent earns reputation-locked rights only after completing paid micro-jobs whose cost exceeds any single payout, so each fake identity is a net loss from day one.
